title: Lead with engaging, real-world expert delivery
difficulty_note: Mostly a positioning change; the volunteer network already exists, but producing testimonials and classroom examples takes production effort.
opportunity: Communicate classroom value; emphasize real-world industry exposure and community volunteers. Position JABC as the organization that connects students with credible professionals and practical, real-world experiences -- not simply as a provider of financial literacy content. Show the presenter experience through testimonials, short videos and concrete classroom examples.

title: Simplify how educators discover, access and navigate programs
difficulty_note: Portal, login and resource architecture -- engineering work, not copy.
opportunity: Simplify the website, program discovery and registration, and the use of the educator portal. Create a clearer path from awareness to program selection, registration and materials: simple grade/subject filters, a visible educator login, clearer onboarding and consolidated resources.

title: Increase awareness through trusted educator channels
difficulty_note: Needs district relationships, PD-event presence and publication slots, plus an owner for the ambassador side -- sustained relationship work rather than a one-off campaign.
opportunity: Increase educator awareness and brand visibility; strengthen district and educator partnerships; increase teacher testimonials and peer referrals; promote on Professional Development days. Expand beyond general outreach by using district communications, educator email, PD events, teacher publications, conferences and administrator networks, supported by staff-meeting materials, peer demonstrations and referral prompts. Educators repeatedly indicated that colleague experience is more persuasive than cold outreach, and that awareness should be built where they already look for trusted opportunities.

title: Make grade, curriculum and student fit immediately clear
difficulty_note: Re-organising and re-labelling an existing catalogue around educator need; no new programme content required.
opportunity: Develop grade- and subject-specific resources; communicate curriculum alignment and classroom value. Organize and communicate programs around educator needs -- such as "for Grade 7 financial literacy" or "for secondary career exploration" -- rather than expecting educators to interpret the broader portfolio.

title: Promote JABC as low-prep, flexible and ready to use
difficulty_note: The offer is already free, facilitated and curriculum-connected. This is stating plainly what is true today -- the cheapest move on the chart.
opportunity: Provide flexible delivery options and promote ready-to-use resources that reduce teacher preparation. Make the teacher value proposition explicit: free, facilitated, curriculum-connected and supported by ready-to-use materials, with concise information on preparation time, session length, educator responsibilities and available follow-up.

title: Communicate at the right time with the right message
difficulty_note: Calendar and template changes to existing comms; no new infrastructure.
opportunity: Communicate at the right cadence for the school year -- late August / early September for annual planning, June for next-year planning, January for second-semester opportunities, and around Pro-D and district planning periods when educators are actively seeking resources. Keep each communication concise and immediately relevant (easy to find information, clear call to action) and reduce email fatigue by not re-sending repeated emails and feedback requests. Explain booking timelines, program steps, required preparation and major platform changes, tailored to the educator's registered program.
mentioned_by: David Welch, Erin Paul, Kimberly Hlina, Sarah Williams, Shannon Soper, Soraya Rajan, Zain Rehmtulla

title: Modernize and tailor content to age, culture and local context
difficulty_note: Re-shooting video, refreshing economic data and building culturally specific variants is production spend, and has to be repeated to stay current.
opportunity: Cultural relevance, local context, modernization of content and age-appropriate tailoring beyond basic grade fit. Refresh examples, videos, design and economic data; test youth-facing content with students; and tailor messaging for specific audiences, including Indigenous learners and students whose pathways may not centre on university or traditional business careers.
